name: Mauscheln
description: Mauscheln (also known as 'Maus' or 'Lurk') is a traditional German gambling and trick-taking game popular in the 19th and early 20th centuries. Similar to games in the 'Rams' family, it focuses on the choice to either 'Sneak' (Mauscheln)—committing to win at least two tricks—or 'Pass' to avoid a penalty. It is famous for its fast rounds, rapidly escalating pots, and the high-stakes risk of the 'Bête' (a penalty equal to the entire pot).

content.text: Mauscheln (also known as 'Maus' or 'Lurk') is a traditional German gambling and trick-taking game popular in the 19th and early 20th centuries. Similar to games in the 'Rams' family, it focuses on the choice to either 'Sneak' (Mauscheln)—committing to win at least two tricks—or 'Pass' to avoid a penalty. It is famous for its fast rounds, rapidly escalating pots, and the high-stakes risk of the 'Bête' (a penalty equal to the entire pot).
Part of the 'Tippen' family of gambling games that spread across Central Europe in the 1700s. Its name 'Mauscheln' suggests speaking in a low, conspiratorial voice or 'sneaking'.

Mauscheln is played by 3 to 5 players. A 32-card German-suited pack is standard; with more players a 52-card French pack may be used. Each player receives 4 cards (dealt 2+2); one card is turned for trump and the remainder form the talon.
32 cards. Ranking: Ace (High), King, Queen/Over, Jack/Under, 10, 9, 8, 7.
Cards; chips or coins for the pot (Pinke).
Dealer places a fixed stake (e.g., 4 coins) in the pot (Pinke). Each player gets 4 cards (2+2). A trump card is turned up.

items.text: Knocking (Klopfen): If dealer turns a high trump (e.g. Ace) before looking at cards, he may knock and become the sneaker; he then discards and exchanges with talon without viewing, then picks up the knocked trump.
Quartets: If dealt a quartet (four of same rank), player must discard them to the bonfire, pay the Pinke, and is dealt a new hand which they may then exchange.
Belli / Weli: Belli: 7 of Diamonds or 7 Bells is permanent second-highest trump after trump Ace; may incur penalty if lost to Ace. Weli: add 33rd card (Weli) as permanent second-highest trump.
